Repo: https://github.com/clawdbot/clawdbot. Source: `src/` (CLI `src/cli`, commands `src/commands`, web provider `src/provider-web.ts`, infra `src/infra`, media `src/media`); tests colocated `*.test.ts`; docs `docs/`; built output `dist/`; plugins `extensions/*`. Keep plugin-only deps in the extension `package.json`; do not add them to the root `package.json` unless core uses them. Installers at `https://clawd.bot/*` live in sibling repo `../clawd.bot` (`public/install.sh`, `public/install-cli.sh`, `public/install.ps1`).

Always consider **all** built-in + extension channels when refactoring shared logic (routing, allowlists, pairing, command gating, onboarding, docs). Core channel docs: `docs/channels/`; code: `src/telegram`, `src/discord`, `src/slack`, `src/signal`, `src/imessage`, `src/web`, `src/channels`, `src/routing`; extensions include `extensions/msteams`, `extensions/matrix`, `extensions/zalo`, `extensions/zalouser`, `extensions/voice-call`.

Docs use Mintlify (docs.clawd.bot). Internal links in `docs/**/*.md`: root-relative, no `.md`/`.mdx` (e.g. `[Config](/configuration)`); cross-references use anchors (e.g. `[Hooks](/configuration#hooks)`). When Peter asks for links, reply with full `https://docs.clawd.bot/...` URLs. When you touch docs, end the reply with the `https://docs.clawd.bot/...` URLs you referenced. README links stay absolute. Docs content must be generic: no personal device names/hostnames/paths; use placeholders like `user@gateway-host` and “gateway host”.

Runtime Node **22+**; keep Node + Bun paths working. Install: `pnpm install`; also supported: `bun install` (keep `pnpm-lock.yaml` + Bun patching in sync when touching deps/patches). Prefer Bun for TypeScript execution: `bun <file.ts>` / `bunx <tool>`. Dev CLI: `pnpm clawdbot ...` or `pnpm dev`; Node supports built output (`dist/*`) and production installs. Build/type-check: `pnpm build`; lint: `pnpm lint`; format: `pnpm format`; tests: `pnpm test`; coverage: `pnpm test:coverage`. Run `pnpm lint` before commits. Run `pnpm test` (or `pnpm test:coverage`) before pushing when you touch logic. Live tests: `CLAWDBOT_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test:live` or `LIVE=1 pnpm test:live`; Docker: `pnpm test:docker:live-models`, `pnpm test:docker:live-gateway`; onboarding: `pnpm test:docker:onboard`. Details: `docs/testing.md`. Vitest/V8 thresholds: 70% lines/branches/functions/statements; tests named `*.test.ts`, e2e `*.e2e.test.ts`.

TypeScript ESM; prefer strict typing, avoid `any`. Add brief comments for tricky logic. Keep files concise; extract helpers instead of “V2” copies; use existing CLI option patterns and dependency injection via `createDefaultDeps`. Aim under ~700 LOC (or ~500 LOC when feasible); split/refactor when useful. Pure test additions/fixes generally do **not** need a changelog entry unless they alter user-facing behavior or the user asks for one.

Product/app/docs headings: **Clawdbot**; CLI, package/binary, paths/config keys: `clawdbot`. stable: tagged releases `vYYYY.M.D`, npm `latest`; beta: `vYYYY.M.D-beta.N`, npm `beta`; dev: moving `main`, no tag. Changelog: latest released version at top, no `Unreleased`; after publishing, bump version and start a new top section. PRs summarize scope, testing, user-facing changes/new flags.

Mobile: before using a simulator, check for connected real devices (iOS + Android) and prefer them when available. Before testing, verify connected real devices before reaching for simulators/emulators. “restart iOS/Android apps” means rebuild (recompile/install) and relaunch, not just kill/launch.

Create commits with `scripts/committer "<msg>" <file...>`; avoid manual `git add`/`git commit` so staging stays scoped. Use concise, action-oriented commit messages; group related changes, avoid unrelated refactors.

PR review: use `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff`; do **not** change branches. Prefer one `gh pr view --json ...` for metadata/comments; use `gh pr diff` only when needed. Before reviewing a pasted GH Issue/PR, run `git pull`; if local changes or unpushed commits exist, stop and alert the user. **Review mode (PR link only):** read `gh pr view/diff`; **do not** switch branches; **do not** change code.

PR merge flow: create a temp branch from `main`, merge PR branch (prefer squash unless history matters; rebase/merge when appropriate). Always try to merge unless truly difficult. If squashing, add PR author as co-contributor. Apply fixes, add changelog entry (+ PR # and thanks), run full gate before final commit, commit, merge to `main`, delete temp branch, end on `main`. If you review a PR and later work on it, land via merge/squash (no direct-main commits) and always add PR author as co-contributor. When working on a PR: add a changelog entry with PR number and thank the contributor. When working on an issue: reference the issue in the changelog. When merging a PR: leave a PR comment explaining exactly what we did and include SHA hashes. For a new contributor, add their avatar to README “Thanks to all clawtributors”; after merging, run `bun scripts/update-clawtributors.ts` if missing, then commit regenerated README.

**Landing mode:** create an integration branch from `main`, bring in PR commits (prefer rebase for linear history; merge allowed when complexity/conflicts make it safer), apply fixes, add changelog (+ thanks + PR #), run full gate **locally before committing** (`pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm test`), commit, merge back to `main`, then `git switch main` (never stay on a topic branch after landing). Important: contributor needs to be in git graph after this! When working on a GitHub Issue or PR, print the full URL at the end of the task.

`sync`: if working tree is dirty, commit all changes (pick a sensible Conventional Commit message), then `git pull --rebase`; if rebase conflicts and cannot resolve, stop; otherwise `git push`.

Web credentials: `~/.clawdbot/credentials/`; rerun `clawdbot login` if logged out. Pi sessions default to `~/.clawdbot/sessions/` (base directory not configurable). Environment variables: `~/.profile`. When asked to open a “session” file, open Pi logs `~/.clawdbot/agents/<agentId>/sessions/*.jsonl` (use `agent=<id>` from Runtime line; newest unless specific ID); for another machine, SSH via Tailscale and read same path.

Never commit or publish real phone numbers, videos, or live configuration values. Use obviously fake placeholders in docs, tests, and examples. Release work: always read `docs/reference/RELEASING.md` and `docs/platforms/mac/release.md`; do not ask routine questions once those docs answer them. Rebrand/migration or legacy config/service warnings: run `clawdbot doctor` (see `docs/gateway/doctor.md`). Vocabulary: “makeup” = “mac app”.

Never edit `node_modules` (global/Homebrew/npm/git installs too). Updates overwrite. Skill notes go in `tools.md` or `AGENTS.md`. When answering questions, respond with high-confidence answers only: verify in code; do not guess. Never update the Carbon dependency. Any dependency with `pnpm.patchedDependencies` must use an exact version (no `^`/`~`). Patching dependencies (pnpm patches, overrides, or vendored changes) requires explicit approval; do not do this by default.

CLI progress: use `src/cli/progress.ts` (`osc-progress` + `<REDACTED_USER>/prompts` spinner); don’t hand-roll spinners/bars. Status tables use ANSI-safe w
